outcome: Detection of critical congenital heart disease
Rate of positive pulse oximetry screens
Rate of false-negative pulse oximetry screens
Location of birth for prenatally diagnosed patients
cohort: The study included 218 live-born patients with critical congenital heart disease born in Nevada between January 2016 and May 2019.
finding: The study identified a high statewide prenatal detection rate (78%) for critical congenital heart disease in Nevada, leading most prenatally diagnosed patients (92%) to be born at a specialized cardiac unit, while universal pulse oximetry screening resulted in more false-negative than positive results.
gest_age: Average gestational age was 38 weeks (+-2.2 weeks)
